classification.difficultyReason: Expand triple angles, simplify quotients and retain the original denominator restrictions.

content.prompt:
Solve the equation
$$\frac{\sin3x}{\sin x}+\frac{\cos3x}{\cos x}=2$$
for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$.

answer.short:
$x=30^\circ,150^\circ,210^\circ,330^\circ$.

Expand the triple angles to obtain $\cos2x=\tfrac12$, retaining $\sin x\ne0$ and $\cos x\ne0$.
answer.worked:
The original equation requires $\sin x\ne0$ and $\cos x\ne0$.

Expand using the sum and double-angle identities:
$$\begin{align*}\sin3x&=\sin2x\cos x+\cos2x\sin x\\\sin3x&=2\sin x\cos^2x+(1-2\sin^2x)\sin x\\\sin3x&=3\sin x-4\sin^3x\\\cos3x&=\cos2x\cos x-\sin2x\sin x\\\cos3x&=(2\cos^2x-1)\cos x-2\sin^2x\cos x\\\cos3x&=4\cos^3x-3\cos x\end{align*}$$

Thus
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin3x}{\sin x}+\frac{\cos3x}{\cos x}&=(3-4\sin^2x)+(4\cos^2x-3)\\\frac{\sin3x}{\sin x}+\frac{\cos3x}{\cos x}&=4(\cos^2x-\sin^2x)\\\frac{\sin3x}{\sin x}+\frac{\cos3x}{\cos x}&=4\cos2x\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}4\cos2x&=2\\\cos2x&=\frac12\\2x&=60^\circ,300^\circ,420^\circ,660^\circ\\x&=30^\circ,150^\circ,210^\circ,330^\circ\end{align*}$$

All four values have nonzero sine and cosine and satisfy the original equation.
